paper.title: Combinatorial Sleeping Bandits with Fairness Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Combinatorial Sleeping MAB with Fairness constraints (CSMAB-F)
unmapped: Set of available arms A(t) drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution and revealed at the start of each round
Long-term fairness constraint: liminf (1/T) sum E[d_i(t)] >= r_i for each arm (minimum selection fraction)
Compound reward is weighted sum of played arms' rewards with known positive weights w_i <= w_max; the learner knows the weights w_i and the fractions r_i
Regret is measured against the optimal fairness-feasible stationary A-only policy (LP solution) and defined as time-average
settings.definition_quote: In each round, the player is allowed to play multiple, but no more than $m$, available arms ... receives a compound reward $R(t)$, which is a weighted sum of the rewards of the played arms ... \liminf_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\mathbb{E}[d_i(t)]\geq r_i \, \, \forall i \in \N

symbols.w_max: upper bound on the known arm weights w_i
symbols.eta: LFG trade-off parameter between virtual queues and UCB estimates

conditions: fairness vector r feasible (comparator is optimal A-only policy satisfying the constraints)

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Under the LFG algorithm, the time-average regret defined in \eqref{eq:regret} has the following upper bound: R_{\text{LFG}}(T) \leq \frac{N}{2\eta} + \frac{\beta_1 \sqrt{mNT\log T}+ \beta_2N}{T}, where $\beta_1 \triangleq 2\sqrt{6}w_{\max}$, and $\beta_2 \triangleq (1+\frac{5\pi^2}{12}) w_{\max}$.

results.notes: Paper bounds time-average regret; multiplied by T to give cumulative. Paper's N (number of arms) mapped to K. Regret defined via means vs R*, hence pseudo-regret. The N/(2 eta) term makes the cumulative bound linear in T unless eta grows.

symbols.eps_slack: positive constant such that r + eps*1 is strictly inside the maximal feasibility region

conditions: r strictly inside the maximal feasibility region C

source.label: thm:feasibility
source.quote: The LFG algorithm is feasibility-optimal. Specifically, for any minimum selection fraction $\mathbf{r}$ strictly inside the maximal feasibility region $\mathcal{C}$, the virtual queue system defined in \eqref{queue} is strongly stable under LFG. That is, \limsup_{T\to \infty} \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \mathbb{E} [\sum_{i=1}^N Q_i(t) ] \leq \frac{B}{\epsilon} < \infty ...

results.notes: Bound on time-averaged virtual queue lengths (fairness constraint satisfaction), not regret; implies the fairness constraints hold in the long run.
